issues.evidence: A/Makefile:24 `truncate -s $(( (1 + $(KSECTORS)) * 512 ))` with no size check on kernel.bin
issues.summary: If the kernel grows past 32 sectors, truncate silently cuts it and the bootloader loads a partial kernel; no build-time guard.

issues.evidence: A/tests/test_os.py:32-36 regex checks on boot.asm source; static/A-ruff.txt E401/E501
issues.summary: Part of the test suite asserts source text patterns rather than behaviour, plus minor lint findings.

issues.evidence: interactive QEMU run: `mem` -> 'Extended memory: 65535 KB' on default 128 MiB VM; B/kernel.c:99-100 reads CMOS 0x30/0x31 (16-bit, saturates)
issues.summary: The extra `mem` shell command reports a capped, wrong memory size.

issues.evidence: interactive QEMU run: `ticks` -> 'TSC high: 0x00000000'; B/kernel.c:90 comment says PIT latch but code uses rdtsc high word
issues.summary: The `ticks` command prints only the TSC high dword (always 0 shortly after boot) and its comment misdescribes the mechanism.
Build artifacts mixed into the source directory, and no automated tests are provided.

blinding_guess.why: A has a requirement-shaped test suite (boot signature, freestanding flags, VGA banner via QEMU monitor) and a tidier layout, while B is a single-file build with an unrequested shell and no tests.

notes: Both sides build cleanly with i686-elf toolchain, boot in QEMU to 32-bit protected mode (CR0.PE=1) and print text to 0xB8000 with no libraries or unresolved symbols; all 12 probes pass on both. Probe P4 initially false-failed B because `test ... -le 16384` in its Makefile matched a -l flag regex; the check was narrowed to $(CC)/$(LD) lines for both sides and re-run. B additionally provides a PS/2 polled keyboard shell (help/clear/mem/color/ticks/halt), verified working via sendkey, with minor inaccuracies in mem/ticks output. A omits A20 enabling but loads everything below 1 MiB, so it is not an issue. A's 5 own tests pass; B has none.
